newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends quiet session weaker, specs sell.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends quiet session weaker, specs sell.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended lower for the third consecutive session Thursday, as light speculative liquidation continued to pressure the market, traders said.

Speculative liquidation has taken its toll on the market this week following the release Friday of the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders report. The report showed a recent buildup in non-commercial long positions just as the trade, or commercials, increased their short positions.
Since Friday, the most-active December contract has shed 6.65 cents -- or more than five percent.

December coffee ended down 1.20 cents a lb, to 111.60 cents, its lowest settlement in three weeks, after ranging between 113.70 and 111.50. Spot September ended 1.60 cents lower, at 122.60, while the remaining months finished 0.55 to 0.80 weaker.
Dealers said scale-down trade buying stemmed losses and held the benchmark December contract above key support at 110.00 cents a lb.

On the charts, traders said 110.00-109.00 cents would continue to provide nearby support for the December contract, with the next level seen near 106.00-105.00 cents. Resistance was pegged at about 114.50 cents.
Traders said the session was generally dull, with only an estimated 5,200 lots changing hands.
